subtopicTitle: Unification — all three theorems as generalized Stokes

cards.front: State the generalized Stokes' theorem for a compact oriented manifold $M$ with boundary.
cards.back: $$\int_M d\omega = \int_{\partial M} \omega$$ where $\omega$ is a differential form of degree $\dim(M)-1$.

cards.front: Which classical theorem is recovered when $M$ is a 1-dimensional interval $[a,b]$?
cards.back: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: $\int_a^b f'(x)\,dx = f(b)-f(a)$.

cards.front: Show how Green's theorem arises as a special case of generalized Stokes'.
cards.back: Let $M\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a plane region and $\omega=P\,dx+Q\,dy$. Then $d\omega=(\partial Q/\partial x-\partial P/\partial y)dx\wedge dy$, so $\int_M d\omega=\iint_M(\partial Q/\partial x-\partial P/\partial y)\,dA=\oint_{\partial M}\omega$.

cards.front: Express the classical Stokes' theorem using the language of differential forms.
cards.back: For an oriented surface $S$ with boundary curve $C$ and 1-form $\omega$, $\int_S d\omega=\oint_C\omega$.

cards.front: Derive the divergence theorem from generalized Stokes' theorem.
cards.back: Take the $(n-1)$-form $\omega=\sum(-1)^{i-1}F_i\,dx_1\wedge\cdots\widehat{dx_i}\cdots\wedge dx_n$. Then $d\omega=(\nabla\cdot F)dx_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_n$, yielding $\int_V\nabla\cdot F\,dV=\int_{\partial V}F\cdot d\mathbf{S}$.

cards.front: What is the degree of the differential form used for each of the three vector-calculus theorems?
cards.back: Green: 1-form in $\mathbb{R}^2$; Stokes: 1-form in $\mathbb{R}^3$; Divergence: 2-form in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

cards.front: Why does the generalized Stokes' theorem require an oriented manifold with boundary?
cards.back: Orientation induces a consistent orientation on $\partial M$ so that the induced boundary integral matches the interior integral of the exterior derivative; without it the equality is undefined.
